newsitem.title: UK: Queen Elizabeth gets golden wedding mug after all.
newsitem.headline: Queen Elizabeth gets golden wedding mug after all.

text.p: One of Britain's foremost china makers on Friday bowed to public demand and decided it would make commemorative mugs to mark Queen Elizabeth's golden wedding anniversary.

Waterford Wedgwood China, which has made royal memorabilia for 238 years, had originally decided to break with tradition and not mark the queen's 50th wedding anniversary in November with special china editions.
But Wedgwood backed down after being bombarded with calls from staunch royalists as far away as Australia.
"We have bowed to public demand. We have made a U-turn after being inundated with calls,' said Wedgwood spokeswoman Clare Elsby. "Designers are now working around the clock," she said.

Wedgwood, which has been marking royal events for the reigns of the last 10 British monarchs, had found that demand for regal souvenirs had waned since it peaked in 1981 with Prince Charles and Princess Diana's fairytale wedding.

The original decision was interpreted in the media as yet another snub to the scandal-tainted House of Windsor, whose popularity has plummeted with each new tabloid revelation of the young royals' marital woes.

Queen Elizabeth, mindful of the winds of change in a society no longer deferential to its monarchy, had decided that the celebrations in November were to be low-key. She adopted a similar approach for her 70th birthday earlier this year.
Aynsley China, Wedgwood's rivals, plan to mark the golden wedding anniversary with a range of memorabilia marketed through a mail order firm.
"The Royal Family are extremely good for us. They have always been a sellout,"

"It is no secret that the royals have undergone a change in people's respect, said Aynsley spokesman Ken Barnes. "But we haven't seen a change as we attract the staunch royalists. Our last two editions have been a sell-out.
"We are already hoping to do editions...for the 100th birthday of the Queen Mother which will of course coincide with the millenium," he added.
The Royal Mint is to mark the anniversary by striking a unique face-to-face gold coin of Queen Elizabeth and her husband, Prince Philip.
It is the first time in the history of modern coinage in Britain that the monarch is not appearing alone on a coin of the realm.
